I want to start by saying that the dentists at this office provide excellent care, especially Dr. Martinez. My concern is specifically regarding my repeated experiences with one dental assistant, Karen.

Unfortunately, I have felt that these questions seem to frustrate her.

I work in a medical office, so wearing scrubs is completely normal for me. The tone of the comment felt sarcastic and inappropriate, and after I responded, she chuckled, which made the interaction feel uncomfortable and disrespectful.

During my daughter’s treatment, after the doctor left the room, Karen removed the gauze from my daughter’s mouth. When saliva came out with the gauze, she commented, “Oh, you’re hungry?” The comment felt unnecessary and made my daughter’s experience less comfortable. We already have concerns about the way she interacts during routine parts of the appointment, including how she handles removing items from my children’s mouths. At times, her reactions make it appear as she is uncomfortable or grossed out by normal aspects of her job. Adding unnecessary comments only makes the experience more uncomfortable for my children.

I understand that everyone can have difficult days or personal challenges, but this has been a repeated pattern of behavior and not a one-time interaction. When working with children and families, patience, kindness, and professionalism are extremely important.

I truly appreciate the care provided by the doctors, especially Dr. Martinez However, based on my repeated experiences, I no longer feel comfortable having Karen involved in my children’s appointments.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and used as an opportunity to improve the patient experience for families. Every child deserves to feel comfortable, respected, and cared for during their dental visits.

⭐ 1/5 — Avoid Oak Tree Property Management

I loved living in my building — until Oak Tree Property Management took over. Since then, it's been a masterclass in how to run a property into the ground.

There is no on-site staff. The leasing office sits empty except during open houses when they're trying to lure in new tenants. Once you've signed, you don't exist.

Their "support line" is an AI pretending to be human. Lock yourself out and call for help, and you get an AI voice service that won't admit it's AI, promises someone will call you back, and no one ever does. If you're lucky enough to reach an actual person, it's an offshore call center that says they'll "forward your request" — into the void. I've locked myself out twice, paid for a locksmith out of pocket both times, and Oak Tree refused to reimburse me either time.

They ignore current residents. I emailed in April about upgrading to a larger unit in June. They said several would be available and promised to follow up. Silence. Apparently they only chase tenants they don't have yet.

Packages are constantly stolen and management does nothing. Under the previous company, we had on-site security and packages didn't go missing. Oak Tree fired the security team AND our beloved on-site staff member — someone who was always there, who once personally helped me during a bathroom flood. Gone.

They gutted amenities. The gym and office used to be 24 hours. Now everything closes at 8 PM. If you work normal hours, good luck ever using what you're paying for.

The building is less secure, less staffed, less accessible, and more expensive to live in (ask me about my locksmith bills). Oak Tree took a great living experience and dismantled it piece by piece. Prospective tenants: what you see at the open house is not what you get. Do not rent any unit from this group

Instead, I received a text the following day stating that my deposit had been refunded. While I appreciate receiving my money back, it did nothing to make up for the stress, inconvenience, and embarrassment of being left without transportation in front of my entire group.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Backstage Limousine. Reliability and communication are essential when booking transportation for a large group, and unfortunately, this company failed on both.

I was headed to San Diego for Comic-Con on a business trip & learned Amtrak runs daily between LA County and San Diego with a stop about 10 minutes from our house. There was a return train the next day, but the site wouldn’t let me book a round trip and I had to get the two tickets separately as two different purchases.

The train was slated to get me to San Diego by 1:30am Sunday morning, which was plenty of time to get to a 10am meeting even allowing for delays.

Bluntly, Amtrak completely, utterly, totally blocked me from getting there as if it was their personal mission. The train arrived at the Van Nuys station roughly on-time, but then they canceled the trip halfway through it. They said the tracks had washed out near Oceanside and the train had to stop in Irvine. The tracks washing out isn’t something they can necessarily control, but a bit of research online revealed that this happens often enough that I feel they should have mentioned that very realistic possibility when I bought the tickets to begin with. They promised buses would come to pick us up and get us to San Diego. Obviously that would mean a delay- understandable.

We’re waiting in silence on the train for what I think was over an hour. Finally, an Amtrak employee informs us over the PA that, due to SDCC, Amtrak Management had decided to not commission buses to complete the trip. (And the wording is important- he went out of his way to say this was a “management decision and not the decision of anyone on the train.”) It’s not that they couldn’t get buses, it was that it was better financially to just ditch us all in Irvine. The other option for passengers was to stay on the train and it would leave "in another 20 minutes" to head back towards LA. I got an automated text and email stating that I would be brought back to my place of origin if I chose to stay on the train.

“Travel Update: As of 12:16 AM PT, Due to track closure stemming from severe washout conditions. Train 794 is now canceled between Irvine (IRV) and San Diego (SAN). All Customers will be returned back to their points of origins.”

At this point, I’m angry that we were promised buses that we’re now told Amtrak just simply decided not to follow-through with. I decided to stay on the train, get brought back to Van Nuys to get picked up and then just drive overnight down to make my commitments.

I then get told by an Amtrak worker (who I’m sure wasn’t having the best night himself, but regardless…) that the train was ending at Union Station in downtown Los Angeles and “No, we are NOT going that far north” (to the Van Nuys stop where I’d started.) They offered no options for what I could do to get home, and made it clear I was on my own after they dumped me in downtown LA in the middle of the night. I had to call my wife and wake her up (again) to ask her to pick me up in LA instead of the station 10 minutes from home and she was supposed to get up at 4:30am for her job.

I am absolutely seething at this point and am just anxious for the train to start moving so I can get home, get to the car and start the drive back south.

The train doesn’t move. For at least another hour, it doesn’t move. The only updates given over the PA is that there are no updates. Finally, they say that the train needs to reverse course, but the computer isn’t working and that’s why we’ve just been sitting here. The train FINALLY starts going back. I exit the train at Union Station and get picked up by my wife (who had to call off work later since she was too exhausted to function properly/safely) and we didn’t get home until after 4am.

I traveled over 7 hours just to end up right back where I started, and Amtrak wasted so much time that they eliminated the realistic possibility of me jumping in the car and driving to San Diego once I finally got home as I was so exhausted at this point that I wasn’t confidant I could drive without dozing off. I had to cancel my entire trip.

This was, without hyperbole, one of the absolute worst customer-service experiences I've ever had with any company in my entire life.
